notes: Gentlest mainstream AHA — good entry exfoliant.
consider_separating: retinoid at the same step on sensitive skin

watchouts.what_to_do: Lower strengths (5-10%) are well tolerated; patch test if reactive.

benefits.concern: dryness / rough texture on sensitive skin
benefits.mechanism: Lactic acid promotes surface desquamation and, as a natural-moisturizing-factor component, increases stratum-corneum water content, so it exfoliates while supporting hydration; controlled AHA trials show improved photodamaged-skin appearance (PMID 8651713).
benefits.what_it_means: Gently smooths and hydrates rough, dry skin — a milder alpha-hydroxy acid suited to sensitive or dehydrated skin.

benefits.mechanism: Gentle acceleration of surface turnover disperses surface pigment and refines the outer layer.
benefits.what_it_means: Brightens dull skin and evens tone with gradual use.

benefits.mechanism: Chronic AHA exposure is associated with modest epidermal and dermal remodeling in controlled trials.
benefits.what_it_means: Supportive smoothing of the look of fine surface lines over time.

evidence.summary: AHA surface-renewal and photodamage benefit shown in double-blind vehicle-controlled human trial (8% lactic arm); humectant role is established NMF chemistry. Graded B.

citations.title: Topical 8% glycolic acid and 8% L-lactic acid creams for the treatment of photodamaged skin: a double-blind vehicle-controlled clinical trial
citations.source: Archives of Dermatology (Stiller et al.); PMID 8651713

overview: Lactic acid gently smooths and hydrates rough, dry or sensitive skin: it promotes surface exfoliation while drawing water into the stratum corneum, making it the AHA of choice for dehydrated or reactive skin.

ingredient.what_it_is: A larger alpha-hydroxy acid (AHA) than glycolic, so it penetrates more slowly and gently. It is also a component of the skin’s natural moisturizing factor, so it doubles as a humectant.

marketing_vs_reality.reality: It does exfoliate more gently than glycolic because of its larger molecule, but it is also a natural-moisturizing-factor humectant, so it supports hydration at the same time — a dual role glycolic does not share.
marketing_vs_reality.claim_in_market: Lactic acid is 'just a gentler exfoliant'
